To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new method to predict the secondary structure of proteins, based on the hydrophobic nature of Gly and its effect on the secondary structure of the protein, which has improved the accuracy of the Chou-Fasmann method.

the modified Chou-Fasnman method is a useful tool to predict the conformations of D1 and D2 polypeptide chains of reaction centre II, which are analogous in structure to L and M chains of reaction centre I.
we have developed a modified Chou Fasman method to predict the con-formation of D1/D1 heterodimer and applied it successfully in the prediction of conformation of the D1/D2 polypeptides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
prediction of protein conformation and its application to study of reaction centre II.
the study of the conformation, stability, and function of the D1/D2 polypeptides in the photosynthetic reaction centres of photosystem II.

the development of a new method for prediction of protein conformation and application of the new method to the prediction of the conformation and the sites for Mn binding in photosynthetic reaction centres.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the D1/D2 polypeptides form an antiparallel beta-sheet with the D2 polypeptide being more hydrophobic than D1.
the modified Chou-Fa-sman method is a good method to predict the secondary structure of the D1/D2 polypeptide heterodimer of thylakoids.

the modified Chou-Faasman method is an improvement over the original method and can be used to predict the conformations of the D1/D2 polypeptide heterodimer and also the conformation of the D1, D1, D3 polypeptides individually.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conformation of the D1 and D2 polypeptide of the photosynthetic reaction center II is predicted to be amphipathic α-helix.
Chou-Fasmans method can be modified to predict the confor- mation of amphipathic polypeptides.

the Chou-Fasmans method has been modified to account for the amphipathic properties of Gly and hydrophilic environment and the modified method has been successfully applied to predict the secondary structures of D1 and D2 polypeptide chains of the photosynthetic reaction center II.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the modified Chou-Fasnman method can be used to predict the conformations of transmembrane polypeptides in the membrane environment and can be applied successfully to predict the confromations of other transmembrane polypetide chains of photosynthetic complexes and other membrane proteins.
Chou-Fasmann method, when modified, is a useful tool for prediction of protein structure.
the modified Chou-Faasman method can be used to predict secondary structure of transmembrane proteins.
